issues.legal_issue: An offence consisting of failure to comply with a lawful direction to remove an obstruction is committed only when the period allowed for compliance expires without compliance.
material_facts: A notice required the respondent to remove an obstruction from a municipal drain and allowed fifteen days after receipt to do so.
The respondent did not remove the obstruction within the allowed period.
The complaint charged failure to comply with the notice, rather than the original erection of the obstruction.
issues.conclusion: The offence, if committed, arose on expiry of the period allowed for removal, and limitation began to run from then; it did not begin on the notice date or the date the obstruction was erected.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 240(1)(b) and 500(1)(b) of the Bengal Municipal Act, 1932, the offence charged is failure to comply with a lawful direction or requisition, not the original erection of the obstruction. A direction to remove an obstruction may allow a reasonable period for compliance, and failure occurs only when that period expires. Accordingly, the limitation period under section 533 begins when the failure first occurs.

predicates.prosecution_for_failure_to_obey_removal_: A prosecution was brought for a person's failure to comply with a direction to remove an obstruction.
predicates.lawful_notice_allowed_time_to_remove: A lawful notice directed the person to remove the obstruction and allowed time for compliance.
predicates.obstruction_not_removed_within_allowed_t: The person did not remove the obstruction within the time allowed by the notice.

issues.definition: When a prosecution concerns failure to obey a lawful removal direction, the direction allows time to comply, and the person does not comply in time, the offence is treated as committed when that time expires.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory limitation period expressed as six months is reckoned in calendar months, not as a fixed period of 180 days.
material_facts: The alleged failure occurred after the period allowed by the notice expired in December 1967.
The prosecution was instituted on June 19, 1968.
The applicable general-clauses legislation defined a month by reference to the British calendar.
issues.conclusion: The six-month limitation period means six calendar months, not 180 days; the prosecution was instituted within that period.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(27) of the Bengal General Clauses Act, 1899 defines a month as a month reckoned according to the British calendar. Therefore, the six-month period in section 533 of the Bengal Municipal Act, 1932 means six calendar months rather than 180 days.

predicates.prosecution_subject_to_six_month_limit: A prosecution is subject to a limitation period expressed as six months.
predicates.applicable_month_definition_uses_calenda: The applicable general definition reckons a month according to the calendar.

issues.definition: Where a prosecution is subject to a six-month limit and the applicable definition reckons months by the calendar, the limit is reckoned in calendar months.
